peer_matches.query_passage: Pune Municipal Corporation has already capped dockless fleets in the old city wards, and a stricter parking rule could force us to build designated parking bays at our own cost. We would reduce this exposure by co-funding thirty marked parking hubs with the corporation and sharing anonymised trip data with its traffic cell, which turns the regulator into a partner rather than an opponent. The second risk is battery degradation. Swap stations cycle batteries harder than overnight depot charging, and if pack life falls below eight hundred cycles the station economics break down. A leasing contract with the battery supplier, priced per kilowatt-hour delivered rather than per pack, moves this risk onto the party that understands the chemistry best.

VoltRide Mobility operates 1,800 dockless electric scooters in Pune and completed 410,000 rides in the last financial year. The founders must decide whether to expand into three tier-2 cities (Nagpur, Indore and Coimbatore) within eighteen months or to deepen operations in Pune by adding battery-swapping stations and corporate subscriptions. Teams must assess market attractiveness, unit economics per scooter, regulatory risk and the funding required for each option. Your submission must recommend one option, justify it with quantitative reasoning, identify the three largest risks and propose mitigation measures for each. Answers should not exceed 1,500 words excluding this prompt. Use only the case exhibits and publicly available sources, and cite every external source you rely on. Submissions will be scored on insight, rigour, feasibility and clarity of communication.
